channel.title: Microbial Metallomics — Blog
channel.description: The metal–microbiome–disease axis: how heavy-metal exposure reshapes the microbiome and drives disease.

item.title: The Metal-Microbiome-Disease Axis: How Heavy Metals May Drive Disease Through the Gut
item.description: Heavy-metal exposure reshapes the gut microbiome, and a disrupted microbiome drives disease. Chain those two well-evidenced links together and you get a mechanistic hypothesis: metals can cause disease through the microbiome. Here is the whole case, link by link, with the strength of the evidence named at each step.

item.title: Arsenic and the Gut Microbiome: A Two-Way Street
item.description: Inorganic arsenic remodels the gut community, and the community in turn governs how much arsenic your body absorbs, transforms, and excretes. The evidence for this bidirectional loop is strong in animals and suggestive in humans.

item.title: Cadmium and the Gut Microbiome: A Hidden Route to Metabolic Disease
item.description: A growing body of animal and human evidence suggests cadmium does not just poison cells directly. It reshapes the gut microbiome, breaches the intestinal barrier, and feeds the metabolic dysfunction that ends in fatty liver and diabetes.

item.title: Feeding the Enemy: How Dietary Iron Reshapes the Gut Microbiome and Raises Enteric Infection Risk
item.description: Most oral iron is never absorbed. It reaches the colon, where it favors enteropathogens over protective bacteria. Randomized trials in African infants show iron fortification remodels the microbiome, inflames the gut, and raises diarrhea risk.

item.title: Does Lead Harm the Developing Brain Through the Gut Microbiome?
item.description: Lead reshapes the gut microbiome in animals and children, and a growing body of work asks whether that dysbiosis is a hidden channel through which lead injures the developing brain.

item.title: Mercury, Methylmercury, and the Microbiome: How Gut Microbes Shape Neurotoxic Risk
item.description: Gut bacteria are active mercury chemists: they demethylate methylmercury and speed its excretion, mercury exposure reshapes the microbiome, and that feedback loop helps set an individual's neurotoxic risk.

item.title: How Low-Dose Heavy Metals May Reshape the Gut Microbiome to Drive Obesity
item.description: A growing body of animal, mechanistic, and human evidence supports the hypothesis that chronic low-dose metal exposure is an upstream, microbiome-mediated contributor to obesity and metabolic syndrome.

item.title: Metals, the Microbiome, and Parkinson's: A Gut-First Pathway to Neurodegeneration
item.description: Manganese, iron, and lead are epidemiologically tied to Parkinson's, and the gut microbiome may be the missing intermediary. Here is the evidence for a metal-microbiome-disease pathway to neurodegeneration.

item.title: How Dietary Nickel Arms Gut Bacteria — and May Fuel Gut Disease
item.description: Nickel is not just a nutrient — it is the cofactor that switches on urease and [NiFe]-hydrogenase in gut Enterobacteriaceae. Here is the evidence linking dietary nickel to necrotizing enterocolitis and IBD, and the gaps that remain.
